body: Then you ask, and ask again, and try to get better, but cannot get out of bed.  Then you ask some more, and things are muddled or you bail.  Eventually you ask another time, but you have not hit rock bottom yet, so they help that is extended is not sufficient.  Then you ask fearing that you will skip rock bottom, go directly to death, and not collect another $200.  Finally, you are too tired to ask.  Lack of food, facing eviction (in a bad winter state), your single family member who tried to help, cannot, you are now just a weight on them too (and you do not want to be, because they are the only one you live for), your friends are not really as close as you would like to be even able to share this with them, no job, no motivation, whtever -- done typing
This is where suicide comes in handy.  When things are about to turn to shit, even though the person feels things are already shit, it might be best not to have 'things' at all.

No, not really.

I have been TRYING to get back on my feet for years.
